prompt: In a circle of radius $9$, an arc has length $6\pi$. What is the measure, in degrees, of the arc's central angle?
hint: What fraction of the full circumference is this arc?

hints.text: What fraction of the full circumference is this arc?

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a half circle: radius $2$ gives circumference $4\pi$, so an arc of $2\pi$ is half the circle, or $180°$. Find the fraction, then take that fraction of $360°$.

learningObjective: Recover a central angle from an arc length.
explanation: The arc is $\dfrac{6\pi}{18\pi} = \dfrac{1}{3}$ of the circle.

alternativeExplanations.title: Or use s = rθ and convert
steps: Both routes work. The fraction-of-the-circle method avoids the conversion, so it is usually faster when the answer is wanted in degrees.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Leaving the answer as 2π/3 ≈ 2.09 — radians in a degree box — is the final-step trap.
The stem says degrees, so the fraction-of-circle route is safest: (6π/18π) × 360 = 120. Match the unit of the answer field, not of your method.
